title: Extended corpus verdicts: udocker F1 fakechroot and ruri work unpatched on the target; rurima/dockless/treesandbox dead at named walls
body:
Second target session (2026-09-07): seven tools tested at their claims, unmodified. Evidence: `verification/real/ext-udocker.txt`, `ext-dockless.txt`, `ext-rurima-ruri.txt`, `ext-treesandbox.txt`. Paper §11a / TOOL.md §2.2 carry the tables.

**Works unpatched:**
- **udocker 1.3.17, F1 (fakechroot)**: pull → `apk add htop/curl` → `curl https://example.com` (HTTP 200) inside `alpine:latest`; volume binds (`-v`); debian glibc binaries run. Requirements: `--allow-root` (euid 0) and `--user=0` — without the latter, fakechroot engines remap user `root` via `HostInfo().username()` → `pwd.getpwuid(0)` → KeyError (no `/etc/passwd`) → `Error: invalid syntax for user`. This is an upstream bug, worked around by the numeric uid. P1/P2 (PRoot) die at `ptrace(TRACEME): Operation not permitted` and misdirect to an Ubuntu kernel bug/`PROOT_NO_SECCOMP`; R1 (runc) exits silently rc=4; dpkg unpack fails under fakechroot (`unable to securely remove '....dpkg-new'` — interposer coverage, paper §10.3's ceiling).
- **ruri 3.9.5**: chroot container over an extracted rootfs; every failed mount/mknod is a per-source-line warning and execution continues; `-u` (unshare mode) is probed and refused cleanly ("Unshare container need at least mount ns support"); apk+curl end-to-end after installing host resolv.conf (ruri doesn't). Trap: `/dev/null` is left absent (mknod EPERM) and the first shell `> /dev/null` silently creates a growing regular file.

**Dead at walls the paper already names:**
- **rurima**: as root, layer extraction uses plain `tar -xpf` → `tar: etc/shadow: Cannot change ownership to uid 0, gid 42: Invalid argument` — the §9.1 unmapped-gid wall, fifth tenant (lilipod tar, containers/storage, Apptainer unpacker, pacman DownloadUser, rurima tar). Its non-root path wraps tar in proot — dead (F). `rurima r` (run a prepared rootfs) works.
- **dockless**: CLI semantics layer behaves exactly as documented (S1 `--rm` guardrail, fail-fast lists, disk precheck, and it independently spots that PATH's `docker` is podman 5.8.2). Engine dead (PRoot/ptrace); hooks/postgres.sh `chown 999:999` → EINVAL and mknod → EPERM (N).
- **treesandbox**: dies before any namespace call (`KeyError: getpwuid(): uid not found: 0`, then missing `/etc/hostname`); architecture is `unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER|NEWNS)`+tmpfs mounts with CHK gates and no fallback — the §8.1 bubblewrap wall.

Consequence for the corpus (paper §11a reading 1): the §10 mode ladder now has unpatched inhabitants on every rung below `namespace` — ruri (chroot), udocker F1 (interpose), pathshim (probe-and-degrade for the notif tier) — so no in-repo patch is needed to demonstrate any mode below namespaces.

title: seccomp-notif supervisor tier is viable on the target; sandlock's --dry-run fails OPEN here (false "no changes" report), pathshim degrades honestly
body:
Second target session (2026-09-07). Evidence: `verification/real/ext-sandlock.txt`, `ext-pathshim.txt`, `extkernel-newapi.txt` §3.

**The tier is viable.** Verified end-to-end on the target with a standalone C probe: installing a further seccomp filter with `SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_NEW_LISTENER` works; the notification round-trip (`NOTIF_RECV` → `USER_NOTIF_FLAG_CONTINUE`) works; `SECCOMP_IOCTL_NOTIF_ADDFD` with `SECCOMP_ADDFD_FLAG_SETFD` injects a supervisor-opened fd into the trapped child, and the child reads it. `/proc/<pid>/mem` of a child opens and preads correctly (read-only). Dead legs: `process_vm_readv/writev` (F) and `/proc/<pid>/mem` O_RDWR (M). Precise viability statement for paper §10.3's supervisor tier: **intercept, read arguments, inject fds — yes; write child memory — no.**

**Field measurements of that boundary:**

- **pathshim** (compforge @ 8bcc34e): `pathshim probe` → `passthrough`, `reason=bind-view-probe-failed error=Operation not permitted (os error 1)`, exit 1; `run` prints the mode line and executes the command unmapped. The failing leg matches its `process_vm_readv` argument reads (src/linux/remote.rs). Honest degradation, exactly as its README documents; its `probe` subcommand is a drop-in preflight for the whole tier.
- **sandlock** (multikernel @ 841265d): the **unsafe direction**. Its notif handlers cannot read the child's path arguments (`process_vm_readv` EPERM) and fall back to Continue — the kernel then executes the syscall directly:
  - `--dry-run` **fails open**: with a `-w` write grant, the sandboxed write reached the file on disk while sandlock printed `dry-run: no filesystem changes` (file content verified changed after exit). Without the grant it fails closed (Landlock denies after Continue).
  - network ACL fails closed: `--net-allow <real-ip>:443` + `curl --resolve` to that IP still blocks (HTTP 000), i.e. allowed traffic is unreachable too.
  - `--chroot`/image modes: exec fails (EACCES dynamic, ENOENT static) — exec remapping requires child-memory writes, both channels denied.
  - What works unpatched: Landlock rulesets (write-allowlist enforced), seccomp-bpf deny stacking, memory limits (`-m 100M` killed a 200 MB alloc), COW-as-direct-write.

Upstream-relevant: a notif supervisor whose per-syscall fallback is Continue should treat child-memory-read failure as a tier-level precondition, not a per-call soft-fail — otherwise advertised safety features (dry-run, COW staging) silently become no-ops on runtimes that filter `process_vm_*`.

Paper §11a reading (2) and TOOL.md §5.9's spec rule ("probe {listener, ADDFD, /proc/pid/mem read} and refuse the tier loudly — never Continue-blind") record this in branch `target-verification-and-lilipod-v2`.

title: F's deny list is larger than §3.2: process_vm_readv/writev filtered; move_mount attach is denied by M (security_move_mount), not the filter
body:
Second target session (2026-09-07) refined the mechanism attributions of §3.2/§3.3. Evidence: `verification/real/extkernel-newapi.txt`, `extkernel-sources.txt`.

**1. F also denies `process_vm_readv` / `process_vm_writev`.**
Both return `EPERM` even for a nonexistent pid (999999), where the kernel would answer `ESRCH` — seccomp cannot fake pid-shaped errnos, so the denial is pre-execution, i.e. the filter. Meanwhile `pidfd_getfd`, `process_madvise`, `kcmp` return `EBADF`/`ESRCH` for bogus args — they execute and are not filtered. Consequence: any supervisor design that reads child memory via `process_vm_*` is dead here; `/proc/<pid>/mem` read-only is the surviving channel (opens and preads correctly; O_RDWR is denied — the M write-allowlist again).

**2. `move_mount` attach is denied by M, not F.**
`move_mount` returns `ENOENT` for a nonexistent destination — proof the syscall executes and the filter does not name it — and `EPERM` for existing targets, both in the initial mount ns and inside a `clone(CLONE_NEWNS)` child we own. Kernel-source attribution (v6.18.39 `fs/namespace.c`, excerpts captured): `move_mount`'s only pre-LSM `EPERM` site is `may_mount()`; `fsmount()` starts with the identical check and **succeeds** on the target, so `may_mount()` provably passes; `do_move_mount()` contains zero `EPERM` sites. The denial is therefore the LSM hook `security_move_mount()` in `vfs_move_mount` — mechanism M. Landlock v6.18 hooks `move_mount`, `sb_mount`, `sb_pivotroot`, `sb_umount`, `sb_remount`, `path_*`, `file_open`, so a single Landlock ruleset is sufficient to explain every M observation to date.

**3. The new mount API splits cleanly (F13):**
- permitted: `fsopen`, `fsconfig(CMD_CREATE)`, `fsmount`, `open_tree(OPEN_TREE_CLONE)`, `mount_setattr` (incl. propagation changes)
- denied: every attach path — `mount(2)`/`pivot_root(2)` by F (bogus-path probes give EPERM pre-execution), `move_mount` by M
- detached mounts are creatable but **unusable**: `openat` on a detached tmpfs/procfs fd → `EACCES` (fstat: root-owned, sticky, world-writable — DAC would allow); an LSM resolving paths cannot resolve a detached mount

Paper §3.2's F-list and §3.7/§9.4 were amended accordingly in branch `target-verification-and-lilipod-v2` (§3.7a, findings F13/F14).

title: Target verification (2026-09-07): settle the two-mechanism model on the real runtime; publish lilipod v2; fix probe verdict bug
body:
Ran the corpus's probes bare on the target runtime the model was built to
imitate, and published the previously-unavailable experimental material.

Settled / corrected:
- identity: /proc/self/uid_map and gid_map are '0 1000 1' with setgroups
  denied, shared with the sandbox init (paper §3.1, §12's open ask).
- bare census on target confirms the attribution table: clone(NEWNS/NEWUSER/
  UTS|NS) permitted; mount, pivot_root, unshare, setns, ptrace EPERM;
  chown/lchown to unmapped ids EINVAL; whiteout mknod OK, real dev EPERM.
- third mechanism found: writes are scoped by path allowlist {/tmp, /dev/shm,
  /workspace, /state} — / and /tmp are both uid-1000 tmpfs mounts with the
  same rw flags, so the mapping cannot explain why only /tmp is writable.
  paper §3.3 row corrected, §3.7 added.
- clone(CLONE_NEWUTS) + sethostname works on the target: per-container
  hostnames are possible; neither manuscript recorded it (§3.7 fact 4).

Second target session (extended corpus, paper §3.7a/§11a):
- mechanism model sharpened: F also denies process_vm_readv/writev; the new
  mount API splits — fsopen/fsmount/open_tree/mount_setattr succeed (so
  may_mount() passes), move_mount attach is denied by M via
  security_move_mount (kernel-source proof in extkernel-sources.txt), inside
  a clone(NEWNS) child too; seccomp user-notification + ADDFD injection and
  /proc/pid/mem reads work (writes denied) — a notif-supervisor tier is
  viable and measured.
- seven tools tested at their claims: udocker 1.3.17 F1 (fakechroot) and ruri
  3.9.5 WORK unpatched (pull→apk install→curl HTTPS; chroot container with
  per-mount warnings); rurima dies at the §9.1 tar wall (5th tenant),
  dockless (PRoot engine + hook contract) and treesandbox (unshare+mount
  architecture) are dead; sandlock's Landlock+seccomp tiers work while its
  notif tier silently degrades — --dry-run fails OPEN with a false "no
  changes" report; pathshim degrades honestly to passthrough and is the
  reference probe for the tier. Evidence: verification/real/ext*.txt.

lilipod v2 (patches/lilipod-restricted-v2.diff + verification/real/):
- exec bug root-caused and fixed: v1's exec path built the enter child with
  cmd.Env = config.Env, stripping LILIPOD_HOME; the child resolved a
  relative store path, fabricated an empty rootfs via MkdirAll, chrooted
  into it and LookPath failed. v2 inherits the parent env. Lifecycle
  evidence incl. working exec captured on the target.
- probe rewritten per §10.2: disposable children, tests the operations
  actually needed (mount-in-own-ns, sethostname-in-own-uts), keeps
  CLONE_NEWUTS when probed — hostname isolation restored.
- Credential{NoSetGroups:true} adopted instead of dropping Credential.

Harness fix:
- probe 'check' now exits non-zero on failure; the 'in clone(NEWNS)' mount
  row used to report the child's exit code (always 0) and said OK above the
  grandchild's FAIL line — visible in results/census.txt and on the target.

Reconciliations:
- runimage pacman.conf ships CheckSpace enabled and no DownloadUser:
  explains the reported /etc/mtab error and installs that worked without
  the model's preconditions (§8.3 note).
- §8.4 misquote corrected: the reported bundle had 0 absolute and 1558
  in-bundle relative links, 26 escaping/dangling dropped — not '26 absolute'.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: lilipod exec bug root-caused & fixed (v2); clone(CLONE_NEWUTS) gives per-container hostnames on the target
body:
Two §5 findings extended by target verification (2026-09-07); patch published in branch `target-verification-and-lilipod-v2` (talaria0101 fork) as `patches/lilipod-restricted-v2.diff` + `verification/real/`.

**1. The residual exec failure (§5.5) is resolved — root cause found by instrumenting the enter child.**
The wrong-root hypothesis was right in shape but the wrong root was *fabricated*: v1's restricted `generateExecCommand` built the enter child with `cmd.Env = config.Env`, which strips `LILIPOD_HOME`/`HOME`. The child recomputed the store from an empty environment, resolved a **relative** store path, `MkdirAll`-ed a fresh **empty** rootfs under its cwd, chrooted into *that*, and `LookPath` failed:

```
EXECDBG: pid=909 cwd="/" rootfs=".local/share/lilipod/containers/<id>/rootfs" command="/bin/echo" stat=no such file or directory
```

Fix: the enter child inherits the parent environment (`RunContainer` applies the container env itself before exec). `exec` now works end-to-end on the target, alongside the full lifecycle (`verification/real/lilipod-v2-lifecycle.txt`).

**2. clone(CLONE_NEWUTS) + sethostname works on the target** — a child in a fresh UTS namespace sets its hostname successfully. lilipod v2's probe (rewritten per §10.2: disposable children, probe the operation needed) keeps `CLONE_NEWUTS` when that succeeds, restoring per-container hostname isolation that both manuscripts reported lost:

```
$ lilipod-v2 exec -i final2 /bin/sh -c 'echo EXEC-WORKS; hostname'
EXEC-WORKS
finalhost
$ hostname   # host, after
sandbox
```

(v2 initially leaked the hostname through the exec path's un-flagged spawn — caught and fixed in the same branch; both spawn sites now use the probed flags.)

Also verified on the target: `main.go`'s `ROOTFUL` default-to-true at uid 0 (§5.3's [S]), which additionally explains the first-run sequence in references/paper-ox.md §4.1.

title: §8.4 misquote: the reported onelf bundle had 0 absolute symlinks (26 were escaping/dangling, dropped)
body:
`paper_final.md` §8.4 states the reported bundle (210 packages) "is said to hold 1,558 relative and 26 absolute links".

The original sanitizer log (references/paper-ox.md lineage) actually reported:

```
absolute->relative: 0, dropped(escaping/missing): 26, ok-relative: 1558
```

i.e. **0 absolute** links existed in the runimage payload, 1,558 relative links resolved inside the bundle and were kept, and 26 relative links that escaped the package root (or dangled outside it, e.g. `etc/mtab -> ../proc/self/mounts` resolving outside `RunDir`) were dropped.

Corrections applied in branch `target-verification-and-lilipod-v2` (talaria0101 fork). The substantive §8.4 point — that the transformation is unauditable without a manifest — stands and is strengthened by the correction.

title: §3.3 'write into uid-1000-owned dir' attribution: target shows a third, path-scoped mechanism
body:
Target-runtime evidence (2026-09-07) falsifies the N-attribution of the writable-directory row for the real runtime.

On the target, `/` and `/tmp` are **both** tmpfs mounts created with `uid=1000,gid=1000`, both `rw`, in a user namespace whose only mapping is `0 -> 1000` — i.e. **both owners are mapped**. Yet:

```sh
$ mkdir /run          # on / (uid-1000-owned tmpfs)
mkdir: cannot create directory '/run': Permission denied
$ touch /tmp/x && echo ok   # on /tmp (uid-1000-owned tmpfs)
ok
```

Mapping cannot discriminate; the writability set is a **path allowlist**: writable exactly {`/tmp`, `/dev/shm`, `/workspace`, `/state`}, denied everywhere else (`/`, `/dev`, `/usr`, `/bin`, `/etc`, `/home`). A seccomp filter cannot implement this (pointer args), and the user-namespace mechanism the paper attributes it to predicts both tmpfs mounts behave alike. This is an LSM-class restriction (Landlock-style allowlist) — a **third mechanism M**.

Evidence: `verification/real/writability.txt`, `verification/real/mountinfo.txt`, `verification/real/identity.txt` in branch `target-verification-and-lilipod-v2` (talaria0101 fork). Paper §3.3 row corrected and §3.7 added there.

The model's own [V] for the model is untouched — this is about the target.

title: probe: 'in clone(NEWNS)' mount row reports the wrong verdict (exit code, not the mount result)
body:
Verification on the target runtime (2026-09-07) exposed a verdict bug in `verification/probe`:

`mount(MS_SLAVE,/) in clone(NEWNS)` re-execs `/proc/self/exe check 'mount(MS_SLAVE,/)'` in the cloned child and returns **the child's exit code**. The child printed the real verdict but always exited 0, so the census row reports `OK` directly above the grandchild's `FAIL errno=1 EPERM` line.

Visible in the published `verification/results/census.txt` (model run) and reproduced on the target:

```
mount(MS_SLAVE,/)                  FAIL errno=1 EPERM   <- grandchild, the true verdict
mount(MS_SLAVE,/) in clone(NEWNS)  OK                   <- exit-code verdict, wrong
```

The §3.4/§8.1 conclusions are unaffected (they rest on the bwrap differential), but the census row is unreliable wherever the mount is denied.

Fix (branch `target-verification-and-lilipod-v2` on the talaria0101 fork): `check` exits non-zero on failure, so the row now reports `FAIL exit status 1`. After the fix, on the target:

```
mount(MS_SLAVE,/) in clone(NEWNS)  FAIL exit status 1
```

consistently with bwrap's `Failed to make / slave: Operation not permitted` on the same runtime.
